text:
support: Peregrine (customer) flagged a sudden p99 latency increase for text-generation calls in us-west-2 since ~12:15 UTC. They saw 300% p99 jump, throughput steady. Attached trace id: trace-0a1b2c. Can runtime folks triage?

devon: thanks — grabbing traces now. Do we know model variant and whether they hit dedicated or hosted?

support: hosted, model redwood-open-13b, autoscaling on. No config changes on their side.

amira: jumping in — first guess is KV cache miss storm or batching fallback. Devon, can you paste the trace?

devon: trace link: https://traces.internal/trace-0a1b2c — root shows long GPU wait at token generation stage (~450ms extra).

lia: can we get queue-depth / batch-size distribution for that timestamp? If batching collapsed to singletons p99 spikes.

marta: pulling metrics from prometheus for host pool in us-west-2. Querying: `sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (pool)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,pool))`

ops-bot: Metric snapshot uploaded: https://metrics.internal/snapshots/2276543210-us-west-2.png (CPU/GPU util + queue depth + kv_cache_hit_rate)

marta: initial look — GPU util was fine (~60%), but kv_cache_hit_rate dropped from 92% -> 24% around 12:14. Queue depth stayed low.

amira: that points to cache TTL invalidation or client prefix variance. Any code deployments that touch cache keys?

devon: checking deploy history... no deploys in runtime or cache service in that window.

lia: ask support if customer ramped traffic with different prompt prefixes (templates can cause cache churn).

support: Peregrine says they did a minor prompt formatting change at 12:10 (switched to include session id in system prompt) — they thought it was safe.

amira: okay that explains low cache hit rate. We should quantify cost/latency delta due to TTL churn and then recommend prefixing best practices. Devon, can you run a small replay with old vs new prompts?

devon: will run an A/B replay on staging using captured requests. Running load: 200 rps for 10m.

marta: while devon runs replay, I'll check whether the KV cache config has protection for high-cardinality keys (we have a feature flag to cap inserts).

ops-bot: Replay job started: replay-227654-rep1 — logs at https://logs.internal/replay-227654


devon: quick snippet I used to replay (for context):

```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-open-13b","prompt":"$PROMPT"}' &
done
wait
```

lia: if replay reproduces p99 bump, we can recommend two mitigations: 1) advise Peregrine to remove session ID from prompt prefix, 2) enable prefix hashing on their Dedicated config (if they were on Dedicated). For hosted, we can add a temporary filter to normalize system prompts for high-cardinality tokens.

amira: can someone open a quick PR to add logging when unique prefix ratio spikes > 5x in 5m window? pinging @sam for a small change.

sam: I can take it. Will add metric and a fallback normalizer behind a feature flag. Should be a tiny change. PR by EOD.

devon: replay finished — hosted staging shows p99 increase ~3.1x when prompts include session ids; median unchanged. KV cache hit_rate drops similarly.

marta: confirmed — cache churn is the culprit. Also saw small uptick in cache insert rate causing slight eviction thrash.

support: communicated to Peregrine to roll back prompt change and they're testing rollback now.

lia: next steps: sam adds spike detector + normalizer; amira to draft recommended prompt guidance; marta to review cache insert cap and consider auto-throttle if unique prefix rate > threshold; devon to collect one more replay after normalizer is live.

amira: I'll post a short note for SRE playbook and customer-facing KB once we confirm rollback improves latency.

sam: creating branch now -> feature/normalize-prefix-spike-detector. I'll link PR shortly.

ops-bot: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/8423 by sam — tests passing in CI.

marta: quick heads-up — if we enable normalizer in prod, need to document opt-out for customers that rely on prompt variation.

support: Peregrine confirms rollback reduced p99 to baseline after 10m. They said thanks.

amira: great. leaving this thread open until sam's change is deployed to staging and we run final replay. If anything regresses, move to #incidents.

sam: deployed to staging under flag `prefix_normalizer=true`. Running validation.

devon: running final replay now.

ops-bot: Replay completed: p99 remains at baseline with normalizer on. Logs: https://logs.internal/replay-227654-final


devon: final check ✅ — p99 baseline restored, cache hit_rate back to ~90%.

amira: thanks everyone. I'll create the KB and link the replay artifacts. Closing after KB published.

support: noted, will follow up with Peregrine and confirm post-mortem email. :thumbsup:
